correctness.rationale: Exact equilibrium reduction gives -xQ/D^2 and the quartic discriminant 12000P. Rational Sturm counts isolate all four P roots and show the negative pair; Q at rho=-131/100 has precisely two roots in (0,1/4). The origin characteristic polynomial and the identity c3=xQ_x/D are independently checked symbolically. On the rational enclosing box, c2>13, |c3|<6 and the two real roots have opposite Q_x signs, yielding exactly one nonzero saddle and one sink by Routh-Hurwitz. A positive-definite weighted quadratic with cubic cancellation has negative-definite derivative iff F>0; discr_a F=120P plus exact root counts and endpoint signs establish this for all rho_f<rho<=0. The nonzero equilibrium at the fold and the unstable origin further left prove sharpness. The included checker was actually run and passed. No unproved global basin claim is made.

originality.rationale: The full October 2026 ETM-3D source studies bifurcations only for nonnegative rho and names the negative branch as future work. The nearest published result gives an exact positive global-stability threshold, and even supplies the same algebraic discriminant and quadratic-Lyapunov mechanism, but explicitly restricts its statement to rho>=0 and does not classify two negative sinks. The exact nontrivial negative bistability interval, indexed saddle, and order of transcritical/fold points are not covered by the accessible compared statements. This is best-knowledge originality, not a proof of worldwide priority.

value.rationale: The original source specifically leaves negative-parameter dynamics unresolved. The exact sharp boundary proves global exponential attraction ends before local origin stability is lost; the intervening parameter interval has exactly two distinct hyperbolic sinks and an indexed saddle. This is a natural hysteresis mechanism with exact algebraic endpoints and a complete local equilibrium census throughout the interval, not merely a computation at a chosen arbitrary parameter or a substitution into an earlier positive theorem.
